1.text:
The surah opens by naming where praise belongs. All praise is for Allah Who created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light: the praise is stated as a fact rather than offered as a wish, and the One praised is named by what He has done, so the reason for the praise is visible in the creation itself. The heavens and the earth are named first because they are the biggest of the things a person can see, and then the same work is described in the pair that governs every day of a life, darkness and light, which are made rather than left to themselves. Then the verse turns from the Creator to the people who are looking at the same world: Yet the disbelievers set up equals to their Lord in worship. The two halves are held together by the word Lord, since the One whose power the first half has just described is the One whose right the second half puts as given to others. Set up equals is a deliberate phrase, because nothing can actually be equal to the Creator, so the setting up is the act of the people and not a fact about the things they worship. The word worship at the end keeps the matter in the open, since what is at issue is not a claim about who made the world but the honour that people give away from the Maker of it. The verses that follow carry the same argument forward, from the creation to the human being made from clay, so this opening serves as the door of the surah. Its shape is worth noticing, a wide statement of what God has done and then a short, blunt account of what people have done with it.

**What praise means here.**

Praise which means to describe in beautiful terms be ever established to God is this meant to be informative so that one believes in it? And on his authority from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's saying (Praise be to Allah) he said: '(Praise be to Allah) Allah says: gratitude and godhood are Allah's, (Who hath created the heavens) in two days: Only Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth from nothing, is described with perfection and praised with the noblest of qualities, and love is only due to Him. One of the great ones of the religion and leaders of the Tariqah said, "Who is worthy of praise other than He whose power created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light? " Who is fitting and who is worthy to be praised for purity and named for greatness other than He who created heaven and earth, created day and night, set up heaven like a roof, adorned earth like a cradle, readied the day for your livelihood, and made the night your time of rest?

**The heavens and the earth, named first.**

By bringing in the sentence which follows immediately, which mentions the creation of the heavens and the earth and the darkness and the light, given there is the very proof of His being the Praised One. Allah praises and glorifies His Most Honorable Self for creating the heavens and earth, as a dwelling for His servants, and for making the darkness and the light to benefit them in the night and the day. The flawlessly regulated revolution of the earth in space around the bright sphere of the Sun and, hence the coming into existence of light and darkness and day and night are events beyond human comprehension. In this verse, samawat' (heavens) has been mentioned in the plural while 'ard (earth), in the singular - though, in another verse (65:12), earth has been identified as being seven like the heavens.

**Darkness in the plural, light in the singular.**

These are three possibilities the most likely of which is the last as the Shaykh Jalāl al-Dīn al-Mahallī states in his commentary on sūrat al-Kahf Q. 181; Who created the heavens and the earth — He singles out these two for mention because for the observer they constitute the most awesome visible creation; and He appointed He created darknesses and light that is every darkness zulma and every light the use of the plural only in the case of the former is because it darkness has many causes; and this is one of the proofs of His Oneness; then those who disbelieve despite the existence of this proof ascribe equals to their Lord they worship others equally. Similarly, by mentioning zulumat' (darkness, or layers of darkness) in the plural, and 'nur' (light) in the singular, the indication given may be that nur or light signifies the correct way and the straight path - and that is just one, while zulumat, or many layers of darkness, signifies the path of error - and their number runs in thousands. In this Ayah, Allah describes darkness in the plural, Zulumat [where Zulmah is singular for darkness], while describing the light in the singular, An-Nur, because An-Nur is more honored. And zulumat (darkness) has been given precedence over nur (light) perhaps because zulumat is basic to this world while nur is associated with particulars - when they are there, there is light; and when they are not there, there is darkness. Also noticeable here is that the origination of the heavens and the earth has been expressed through the word, 'khalaqa' (created) while that of darkness and light with the word, ja‘ala' (made). Tuesday and Wednesday, (and has appointed darkness and light) He created faith and disbelief or night and day. He created the night and the day, which follow one another.

**One Maker, and the many that were worshipped.**

By saying in this verse of the Holy Qur'an that Allah Ta ala is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and He is the Maker of darkness and light, all such false notions have been refuted - when He is the sole Creator and Maker of everything, ascribing partners to His Divinity makes no sense. As for the disbelievers and polytheists of Arabia, they demonstrated such philanthropy in dishing out Godhood that, according to them, every piece of rock on a hill could be good enough to become an object of worship for the whole human-kind! Thus, the wonderful human being whom Allah had made to be the noblest of His creation, someone whom the whole universe was to serve, went so astray from the right path that he took - not just the moon, the sun, the stars, but the fire, water, trees and rocks too - even crawling insects as objects of prostration and worship, providers of needs and resolvers of problems.

**The servants who give the worship away.**

(Yet those who disbelieve hold others as equal with their Lord.) meaning, in spite of all this, some of Allah's servants disbelieve in Him and hold others as partners and rivals with Him. Despite all this, some of His servants disbelieve Him and associate partners with Him. Meaning, it is He Who is called Allah, throughout the heavens and the earth, that is, it is He who is worshipped, singled out, whose divinity is believed in by the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. (It is He Who is God in the heavens and the earth.)[43:84] meaning, He is the God of those in heaven and those on earth, and He knows all affairs, public and secret.

2.text:
He is the One Who created you from clay, then appointed a term for your death and another known only to Him for your resurrection, yet you continue to doubt. The verse follows the opening praise by turning to the human being, and it moves in three steps. He is the One Who created you from clay names the beginning, and the clay is the same material the reader stands on, so the argument starts where the reader is, with a body taken from the ground. Then the second step: then appointed a term for your death and another known only to Him for your resurrection. One term is set for the end of each life, and a second term is kept out of sight, and the wording draws attention to the difference, since the first is known to the people who live through it while the second is known to the Creator alone. The order of the two is part of the argument, because the One who began the making is the One who has set both limits, so the raising at the end stands with the first creation rather than against it. Then yet you continue to doubt, which names the response of the people addressed. The doubt is not about the creation they can see but about the second term, and the verse leaves the two side by side, the making that is admitted and the raising that is questioned, so that the reader feels the wrongness of the position. The verses that follow stay with the same human being, and the rest of the surah returns to this pair of subjects, so the verse sets a pattern rather than making a single point.

**Created from clay.**

It is He Who created you from clay by creating your father Adam from it; then He decreed a term for each of you at the conclusion of which you die. (He it is Who has created you from clay,) refers to the father of mankind, Adam, from whom mankind originated, multiplied in numbers and spread about, east and west. He, may He be glorified, is the One Who created you, O people, from clay when He created your father, Adam ﷺ from it. (He it is Who hath created you from clay) i.e. from Adam and Adam was created from clay, (and hath decreed a term for you) He created this world and fixed a term for its extinction and made created beings whose lifespan expires with death. The verse is saying that Allah is the One who created Sayyidna Adam with clay, and then, gave him life - and common human food comes from the moist substance of clay, and from food the sperm, and from the sperm comes the creation of the human being.

**The term set for death, and the term kept with Him.**

A term is stated fixed with Him for your resurrection; yet thereafter you O disbelievers doubt you are uncertain about the Resurrection when you know that it was He Who initiated your creation and One Who has the power to initiate creation is even more capable of bringing you back to life after death. After that, comes the mention of the end of the whole world, that is, the Qiyamah, in the following words: , that is, there is yet another term which stands fixed and which is known to Allah alone. (Then has decreed a stated term,) refers to death, while,. (And there is with Him another determined term...) refers to the Hereafter, according to Sa'id bin Jubayr who reported this from Ibn 'Abbas. (And then has decreed a stated term,) is the term of this earthly life, while,. (And there is with Him another determined term) refers to man's extent of life until he dies as mentioned in Allah's statement;. (It is He, Who takes your souls by night (when you are asleep), and has knowledge of all that you have done by day, then He raises (wakes) you up again that a term appointed (life) be fulfilled.)[6:60] The meaning of Allah's statement,. (They ask you about the Hour – when will be its appointed time? You have no knowledge to say anything about it. To your Lord belongs (the knowledge of) the term thereof.)[79:42-44] Allah said,. The expression - the personal end of a human being' - is used here because Allah Ta ala destined a term for his or her life (on the earth). Reaching the completion of this term is death - though human beings do not know it - but, the angels do. The full knowledge of this term' has not been given to any angel, or human being. (A term is fixed with Him) Allah knows the term of the Hereafter: therein there is no death or evanescence. Then He, may He be glorified, fixed a period for your stay in the life of the world. He also fixed another term, which only He knows, when He will raise you back to life on the Day of Rising.

**The doubt the verse names.**

Despite this, you still doubt about His ability to raise you back to life. (Yet still you) O people of Makkah (doubt) in Allah and resurrection after death! The words: ‌ (And the fixed term lies with Him, yet you are in doubt) carry the instruction that using the personal death of a human being as the proof of the general and collective death of the whole world system, that is, the Qiyamah, is something very natural and logical. Then, it is to shake human beings out of their negligence that they have been told that every human being has a particular age, after which death is certain. Therefore, there is absolutely no doubt about the coming of the Qiyamah (the much publicized but least believed Apocalypse' of the West).

**The clay of the human being, and what was breathed into it.**

His clay pertained to the World of the Creation, and his spirituality to the World of the Command. What pertains to creation is "He fermented Adam's clay in His hand. " What pertains to the command is I have blown into him of My spirit [15:29]. In Adam were both rose garden and field of clay, so the clay was the place of roses. The body of a human being is wholly made of earth elements but it has unique properties, none of which is found in the earth. From earthen elements a non-earthly creature has wondrously emerged.

**The world of the Hereafter, from the matter of this world.**

In such circumstances, man is unable to understand how the eternal world of the Hereafter, which will be free from grief ( 35:34) can come into existence. If the world of the Hereafter is to be created with some matter other than that of this world, that is something beyond man’s ken; but if the other world of the Hereafter is to be created from the matter of this world, it has to be conceded that this world in itself lacks the capacity to bring into existence a world of total perfection. If a living and active man comes into existence from earth; if fragrant flowers and luscious fruits emerge from earth, then why cannot a more perfect world emerge from our present world?

3.text:
He is the Only True God in the heavens and the earth. The verse carries the argument forward by naming the One who is worshipped above and below, and the phrase only true is the key to it, since it excludes every partner at once rather than listing them one by one. He knows whatever you conceal and whatever you reveal: the knowledge is stated in the same breath as the worship, and the pair hidden and revealed covers the two directions a person's life takes, what no one sees and what everyone sees. and knows whatever you do: the last clause widens the account from words to acts, so the verse closes on the whole of a person's conduct. The order is worth noticing, since the worship is stated first as the right of the One described, and the knowledge then follows as the reason the claim reaches every life, including the parts that are not shown. The two halves hold each other up, because a Lord of the heavens and the earth who did not know what people conceal would not be the Lord the verse names, and a knowledge that saw everything but claimed no worship would not be the demand the verse makes. The verses before had named the creating and the doubt, and this verse answers the doubt with knowledge, so the reader is taken from the world outside to the inside of the self. The verses that follow take up the signs that were disregarded, so the mention of what is hidden prepares the reader for a passage about what people turn away from.

**The One worthy of worship in both worlds.**

He is God the One worthy of being worshipped in the heavens and in the earth. It declares that Allah is the only Being who is worthy of worship and obedience in all the heavens and the earth, and He is the One who knows everything human beings conceal or reveal and, particularly, everything they say or do. (He is Allah in the heavens) He is the God of the dwellers of heaven (and in the earth) and the God of all the dwellers of the earth. He, may He be glorified, is the One worthy of worship in the heavens and the earth. Meaning, it is He Who is called Allah, throughout the heavens and the earth, that is, it is He who is worshipped, singled out, whose divinity is believed in by the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth.

**What you keep secret and what you make public.**

He knows your secrets and your utterance what you keep secret and what you utter openly among yourselves and He knows what you earn what you do of good and evil. He knows what you keep hidden in your breasts just as He knows what you make public, (and He knoweth what you earn) of good or evil. He knows the intentions, statements and actions you keep hidden and those you make public; and He will judge you about them. (It is He Who is God in the heavens and the earth.)[43:84] meaning, He is the God of those in heaven and those on earth, and He knows all affairs, public and secret.

**The earth, and the human being made from it.**

The body of a human being is wholly made of earth elements but it has unique properties, none of which is found in the earth. Man hears; he speaks; and he thinks; he performs wonderful acts, though the earth with which he is made is not capable of performing these acts. From earthen elements a non-earthly creature has wondrously emerged. If a living and active man comes into existence from earth; if fragrant flowers and luscious fruits emerge from earth, then why cannot a more perfect world emerge from our present world? He who sees You is concealed in vision, and he who seeks You is neither on earth nor in heaven.

**Where the surah was revealed.**

The Virtue of Surat Al-An'ām and When it Was Revealed. Al-'Awfi, 'Ikrimah and 'Ata' said that Ibn 'Abbas said, "Surat Al-An'am was revealed in Makkah" At-Tabarani recorded that Ibn 'Abbas said, "All of Surat Al-An'am was revealed in Makkah at night, accompanied by seventy thousand angels, raising their voices in glorification of Allah" As-Suddi said that Murrah said that 'Abdullah said, "Surat Al-An'am was revealed in the company of seventy thousand angels."

4.text:
Whenever a sign comes to them from their Lord, they turn away from it. The verse is short and it makes one movement, and the shape of that movement is the teaching. The first half states the coming of the sign: whenever a sign comes to them from their Lord, and the wording is general, so it is not one sign that has been refused but every sign that arrives, and the sign is named as coming from their Lord, which makes the refusal personal rather than a difference of opinion about evidence. The second half states the response: they turn away from it, and the turning away is described as an act of the body, an about face, rather than a failure to understand. The word that joins the two halves is the hinge of the verse, since it makes the arrival of the sign the occasion of the refusal rather than its cure, and the reader is shown people who are met by the proof and walk off from it. The verses that come before had named the creating and the knowledge, and this verse begins a run of the same account, so the reader is being readied for what the surah will say about the signs and the mocking of them. Nothing in the verse describes the size of the sign or its kind, and the general wording keeps it that way, so the charge is not that a particular proof was not strong enough but that the pattern is fixed.

**The sign their Lord sent.**

‌ ‌ 4 that is, despite the many clear proofs and open signs of the Oneness of Allah, the dissenters and rejectionists among human beings have taken to a way of their own, using which, they would turn their faces away from whatever sign is shown to them for their guidance, without ever paying the least attention to it. (Never came there unto them) i.e. unto the people of Makkah (a revelation of the revelations of Allah) such as the eclipse of the sun or the splitting of the moon or stars (but they did turn away from) except that they disbelieved in i.e. the sign. No proof or miracle from their Lord comes to the idolaters except that they ignore it without paying any attention. The message of God and the Hereafter, issued directly by God Himself, is accompanied by clear signs which establish it as a true call from the Almighty.

**The signs and those who turn from them.**

Clear evidences and proof of the Oneness of Allah, as well as miracles proving the truthfulness of the messengers, have now come to them; yet despite this, they turned away and paid no attention to these signs and miracles. When these signs come to a man’s attention, he attributes them to certain causes and pays no heed to them. Allah states that the rebellious, stubborn polytheists will turn away from every Ayah, meaning, sign, miracle and proof that is evidence of Allah's Uniqueness and the truth of His honorable Messengers. The reason for this is that all these proofs, in spite of all their clarity, always appear through a veil of cause and effect.

**The generations before them.**

And never an Ayah comes to them from the Ayat of their Lord, but that they have been turning away from it Indeed, they rejected the truth when it came to them, but there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock at Have they not seen how many a generation before them We have destroyed whom We had established on the earth such as We have not established you? (Have they not seen how many a generation before them We have destroyed whom We had established on the earth such as We have not established you?) meaning, they had more wealth, children, buildings, abundant provision, riches and soldiers. Yet We destroyed them for their sins, and created after them other generations. (and created after them other generations,) for, these generations of old perished and became as legends and stories,. (And created after them other generations.) so that We test the new generations, as well.

**The earth, and the world that comes after.**

The body of a human being is wholly made of earth elements but it has unique properties, none of which is found in the earth. Man hears; he speaks; and he thinks; he performs wonderful acts, though the earth with which he is made is not capable of performing these acts. From earthen elements a non-earthly creature has wondrously emerged. If a living and active man comes into existence from earth; if fragrant flowers and luscious fruits emerge from earth, then why cannot a more perfect world emerge from our present world? Allah advises and warns the disbelievers, that they should avoid the torments and afflictions of this life, similar to what befell their likes from previous nations, who were stronger, wealthier, had more offspring, and were more exploitive on the earth.

5.text:
They have indeed rejected the truth when it came to them, so they will soon face the consequences of their ridicule. The verse closes the accusation that the ones before it had begun, and it does so with two clauses that stand as cause and outcome. The first clause states the act: they have indeed rejected the truth when it came to them, and the emphasis falls on have indeed, so the rejection is treated as settled and not as a possibility. The truth is not named in detail, and the time named is when it came to them, which puts the refusal at the moment of arrival rather than after long thought. The second clause then states what follows: so they will soon face the consequences of their ridicule, and the shape of the sentence keeps the two ends tied together, since the thing they laughed at is the thing that will meet them. The word soon takes the outcome out of the distant past and puts it in front of the reader, and the phrase the consequences of their ridicule is wide enough to cover both the news they will hear and the punishment they will taste. The mocking itself is left unnamed, which is how the surah has treated it from the first signs, and the reader is left with the pattern, a sign, a turning away, and then an accounting that arrives on its own time. The verses that follow carry the same account on with the generations who were stronger and the challenge that was left unanswered, so this verse stands at the head of a passage about what happens to those who refuse what has reached them.

**The truth they rejected.**

They denied the truth the Qur’ān when it came to them but there shall come to them the news the consequences of what they were mocking. (And they) the people of Makkah (denied the Truth) the Qur'an and the sign (when it came unto them) when Muhammad ﷺ came to them. This Ayah contains a warning and a stern threat for the disbelievers' rejection of the truth, stating that the disbelievers will surely know the truth of what they used to deny and taste the evil end of their behavior. While they have turned away from these clear evidences and proofs, they had previously turned away from something even clearer: they denied the Qur’ān that Muhammad ﷺ brought.

**What they used to mock.**

It means that right now these people who are heedless to their fate mock at the miracles and commandments of Allah brought by the Holy Prophet and at the all true message that there is a Qiyamah (Doomsday) and Akhirah (Hereafter), but very soon will come the time when all these realities will be before their eyes. They will soon realise, when they see the punishment on the Day of Rising, that what they used to mock and what he brought to them was in fact the truth. (But there will) this is a threat of punishment (come unto them the tidings of that which they used to deride) the news of their derision and the punishment of their derision on the Day of Badr and the Day of Uhud as well as on the Day of the Confederates. But his' antagonists, who would have not hesitated to sacrifice anything they had - life, wealth, honour, children, family, anything, anytime - just to defeat him, did not have the courage to accept his challenge and, at the least, produce one 'Ayah (verse) like the 'Ayah of the Holy Qur'an. Now, pointed out at the conclusion of the verse is the sad end of their effort to falsify truth: The word, Al-Haqq' (the truth) here, could mean the Qur'an - and the blessed person of the noble Prophet also.

**The reckoning and the retribution.**

There will be a Reckoning (Hisab) when everyone will have to account for one's faith and deed - and everyone shall get the reward or punishment for what he or she has done. But, believing and confessing at that time is not going to work for them because that will be no day of deeds - rather, that day will be the day of Retribution.

**The generations before them.**

(Have they not seen how many a generation before them We have destroyed whom We had established on the earth such as We have not established you?) meaning, they had more wealth, children, buildings, abundant provision, riches and soldiers. (and created after them other generations,) for, these generations of old perished and became as legends and stories,. (And created after them other generations.) so that We test the new generations, as well. Yet We destroyed them for their sins, and created after them other generations. The succeeding generations repeat those very same actions as were indulged in by their predecessors, due to which they were destroyed. The recurrence of events in which one set of people face decline while another set rises shows that the rule of ‘crime and punishment’ is prevalent here, but man does not learn a lesson from this.

6.text:
The verse puts a question to the people who had heard the message and had not answered it: Have they not seen how many disbelieving peoples We destroyed before them. The question is not a request for information but a demand that they look, and the word seen means to consider and to draw a conclusion rather than to watch with the eye. The peoples named were destroyed, and the destroying is put first so that the reader knows where the account ends before hearing how it began. Then the verse describes what those peoples held before they fell: We had made them more established in the land than you. The establishment is named in the land itself, so the advantage is one the reader can see, and the comparison closes with you, which turns the account into a mirror for the people addressed. Then the third phrase: We sent down abundant rain for them and made rivers flow at their feet. Rain in abundance and rivers running at their feet are the signs of a settled and well watered life, and the verse gives them as provisions from the same hand that later took them away. Then the last phrase: Then We destroyed them for their sins and replaced them with other peoples. The sins are named as the cause, so the outcome is not arbitrary, and the replacing shows a world that does not stand empty, since one people goes and another takes its place. The four phrases are ordered as a lesson rather than as a record: the question, the advantage, the provision, and the end. The reader is meant to notice that the people who were given more than the reader has were not spared, and that the comparison is not between the past and the present but between what people do with what they are given. The verses that follow turn to a particular demand from the people of Makkah, so this passage has done the work of setting the ground before it.

**The peoples destroyed before them.**

(See they not) were the people of Makkah not informed in the Qur'an (how many a generation) past nations (We destroyed before them, whom We had established) We gave them sovereignty and respite (in the earth more firmly than We have established you) than the sovereignty and respite We have given you, O people of Makkah, (and We shed on them abundant showers from the sky) whenever they needed it, (and made the rivers flow beneath them) beneath their fields, plantations and trees. Then We destroyed them because of their sins because of their denial of the prophets; and We raised up after them another generation. Even historic instances of God’s having destroyed materially well set up people, as if their lives were of no value whatsoever, fail to teach them a lesson. (Yet We destroyed them for their sins) We destroyed them because of denying the prophets, (and created after them another generation) a different people who were better than they. Do these disbelievers not know Allah’s custom of destroying communities who do wrong? In the present verses, the same deniers of the truth have been given an opportunity to learn and correct themselves by observing conditions around them as well as those prevailing in times before them.

**The power and the strength they were given.**

About past peoples of the world, first it was said that the kind of power and well-being given to them was not given to people later than them, but when these very people took to the ways of belying prophets and disobeying Divine injunctions, all that majesty of power and wealth was rendered futile against the punishment of Allah which annihilated them totally. It means that the great power of Allah Jalla Sha'nuhu was not simply limited to seeing that nations of strength, authority and power lay destroyed in a flash, but it was right there on the ashes of their destruction that other peoples were made to rise and populate places, as if nothing had happened there and no one was missing from the scene. In the first verse, it was said about the people of Makkah, the direct addressees of the Holy Prophet : ‌ ‌ Havethey not seen how many generations We have destroyed prior to them?' Here, seen' means to ponder about, because these generations were not present before them at that time to see. (Have they not seen how many a generation before them We have destroyed whom We had established on the earth such as We have not established you?) meaning, they had more wealth, children, buildings, abundant provision, riches and soldiers. So, this was a lesson for the addressees of today, the people of Makkah who did not have the power of the legendary people of Ad and Thamud, nor the affluence of the people of Syria and Yaman. This spectacle of Divine power and wisdom is something observable in its own ways during every time and period when thousands die every day but there is no vacuum left anywhere. Therefore, beware of the same end that might befall you, for you are not dearer to Allah than these previous nations, but the Messenger whom you defied is dearer to Allah than the Messengers they defied. Thus, you are more liable than them to receive torment, if it was not for Allah's mercy and kindness.

**The rain and the rivers.**

Have they not seen in their travels to Syria and to other places how many kam is predicative and not interrogative meaning ‘many’ a generation how many a community of past communities We destroyed before them; We established them We assigned them an established place in the earth through strength and abundance as We have not established as We have not assigned you there is a shift in the address here from third person to second; and how We unleashed the heaven the rain upon them in torrents one torrent after another and made the rivers to flow beneath them? beneath their dwellings. (and We poured out on them rain from the sky in abundance,) in reference to rain that comes often,. (And made the rivers flow under them.) as rain was abundant and the springs were plentiful, so that We deceived them. Allah sent down successive rains upon them and made rivers flow beneath their homes; yet they then went against Him, so He destroyed them because of the sins they committed.

**A lesson that was not learnt.**

No doubt, events of the past are documents full of chastening lessons which, if seen to find wisdom, would prove to be more effective than a thousand sermons. This may be indicative of the reality that a report or story is not an end by itself, instead, the purpose is to identify the outcome of the report and the practical implication of the event, therefore, one should be concerned with what is necessary for the objective in sight, move ahead and survey his circumstances in that light - that is, learn that vital lesson from what has gone before and thereby correct oneself. For them, the need of the hour was to learn a lesson from what happened to the peoples of the past and turn towards an examination of their doings and think where they are going to end up by op-posing the truth. They have, rather than benefiting from it, made it into an intellectual pastime which would either help to sleep or to while away spare time. But, speaking generally, people have not given world history any serious role in conducting lives properly. (Yet We destroyed them for their sins) meaning the mistakes and errors that they committed,.

**The generations that came after them.**

(and created after them other generations,) for, these generations of old perished and became as legends and stories,. (And created after them other generations.) so that We test the new generations, as well. Yet, they committed similar errors and were destroyed, as their ancestors were destroyed. It was after that, that the destruction of many generations ( qarn') was mentioned. The word, qarn, is used for a group of people collectively present at a given time and period. At the end of the verse, it was said: ‌ ‌ (and raised up, after them, another generation). Those who have firmly established themselves in this world, having accumulated many material goods for themselves, and who see the manifestations of their own greatness and popularity around them, are always liable to be a prey to misunderstanding. This overweening confidence on their part increases to such an extent that they even become unafraid of God. Once, while on the plains of Arafat with a million men and women spread around, came the thought that only a mere seventy or eighty years earlier, none among this whole assembly of people existed.

7.text:
The verse answers a demand that had been put to the Prophet with a picture of what would happen even if the demand were met. Had We sent down to you O Prophet a revelation in writing and they were to touch it with their own hands: the writing is named as a thing on a page, and the touching is added to it, so the proof would arrive with the strongest of the senses behind it and no room left for doubt about what was placed in front of them. Then the sentence turns: the disbelievers would still have said. The turn is the whole point of the verse, since the answer is not that the sign would be too hard to make but that the objection was never about evidence. Then their words: This is nothing but pure magic. Magic is the one explanation that lets a person set aside what he sees without denying it, and the wording shows how little the demand had to do with being convinced. The order matters, the sending down, the touching, the speaking, and then the name they would give it, and the last phrase undoes the first three. The verse before had ended with the destruction of peoples who held more than those who came after them, and this verse continues in the same voice, dealing with a people who asked for proof and were given a warning instead. The verses that follow take the same demand on step by step, so this is the first answer to it and the sharpest one. Nothing in the verse states that the sign was ever sent; the form is conditional from beginning to end, and the reader is left with the stubbornness rather than with the sign.

**The demand for a book from the heavens.**

The second verse was revealed in the background of a particular event when Abdullah ibn Umaiyyah came up with a hostile demand before the Holy Prophet by saying: I cannot believe in you until such time that I see you climbing all the way to the heavens and bringing a book from there before our eyes, in which it should be written in my name that I should attest to your prophethood.' And, on top of saying all this, he went on to even declare that he would still not be impressed enough by his accomplishing all that for he does not seem to be likely to convert to Islam anyway. If we had sent down to you, O Messenger, a book written on paper and they had seen it with their eyes, they would not have accepted it out of stubbornness and denial; and they would have said, ‘What you have brought is nothing more than clear magic; and we will never believe in it’. O Muhammad, by Allah we will not believe until you bring us a book from Allah along with four angels with it, bearing witness that it is from Allah and that you are His messenger , and so this verse was revealed . They were a kind of people who would not stop at what they were demanding. Such were the uncalled-for and hostile demands made and mocking and insulting dialogues inflicted on the Holy Prophet especially when he himself was more affectionate for his people, more than their own parents could ever be to them.

**The hands that would not believe.**

(And even if We had sent down unto you a Message written on paper so that they could touch it with their hands,) meaning, if they saw this Message's descent and were eye-witnesses to that,. For example, if Allah were to send down, as they demanded, a written book from the heavens - and not only that they see it for them-selves that there is no sleight of hand or sight or magic, they may even physically touch it with their hands to make sure that they were not day-dreaming and that it was a reality - still, after all that, they would say nothing but: And had We revealed to you a Scripture inscribed on parchment as they requested and had they then touched it with their hands — this is more powerful than saying ‘had they seen it with their eyes’ since it touch is more effective in eliminating doubt; the disbelievers would have said in disobedience and obduracy ‘This is nothing but manifest sorcery’.

**Nothing but magic.**

(Had we sent down unto thee (Muhammad) if Gabriel had brought down the Qur'an to you in one bulk ((actual) writing upon parchment) as asked for by 'Abdullah Ibn Umayyah al-Makhzumi and his friends, (so that they could feel it with their hands) so that they would hold and read it, (those who disbelieve) i.e. 'Abdullah Ibn Umayyah al-Makhzumi (would have said: This is naught else than mere magic) a clear lie. (the disbelievers would have said: "This is nothing but obvious magic!") This is similar to Allah's description of the disbelievers' defiance of facts and truth,. Similarly, if a book complete in every detail, comes down from the sky, he will say, ‘This is mere magic,’ to justify his rejection of it.

**What the sending of an angel would mean.**

(Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been judged at once, and no respite would be granted to them.) (We send not the angels down except with the truth (i.e. for torment, etc.), and in that case, they (the disbelievers) would have no respite!)[15:8], and,. Consequently, even if the angels descend, while the disbelievers still had the same attitude, then the torment will surely befall them from Allah as a consequence. (On the Day they will see the angels, no glad tidings will there be for the criminals that day.)[25:22] Allah's statement,. In this case, the angel (in the shape of a human) will also cause confusion for them, just as the confusion they caused themselves over accepting humans as Messengers!

**The messengers who were mocked before him.**

It is a mercy from Allah to His creation that He sends every type of creation, Messengers from among their kind, so that they are able to call their people to Allah, and their people able to talk to them, ask them and benefit from them. In the present world, because of their devotion to externals, people are unable to recognise the Messenger of God from the importance of his message. God’s Messenger appears to them like an ordinary man suddenly emerging and claiming very high status. (And they say: "Why has not an angel been sent down to him?") to convey the Message with admonition along with him. If the hidden realities were revealed and God and His angels made their appearance, there would be no question of prophethood or of giving the call of Truth, because thereafter nobody would dare to deny the realities. This is because what they are saying comes from malice and hostility. Therefore, to comfort him, it was said that such demands from his antagonists were not being put forward for any useful purpose, nor did they want to follow it.

8.text:
The verse carries the demand one stage further, and then answers it with a condition. They say, Why has no visible angel come with him: the question is quoted as theirs, and the word visible is the whole of it, since the askers wanted a messenger whose coming no one could miss. Then the answer begins with the same conditional shape as the verse before: Had We sent down an angel, and the coming of the angel is left as something that did not happen, which is the mercy the passage is building towards. Then the clause that explains why, the matter would have certainly been settled at once. Settling is the word for a judgement that ends the discussion, and at once removes the interval in which a person can think again. Then the last phrase: and they would have never been given more time to repent. The verse keeps the two halves of the answer together, since the sending would have been followed by a sentence, and the time in which they now live is the thing being protected. The verses before had named the handing over of a book and the answer the disbelievers would give, and this verse treats the demand for an angel in the same way, so the reader sees a pattern rather than a series of separate requests. The demand itself is left without a name for the person making it, which is how the passage has handled the questioners throughout. The verse that follows takes the same condition and follows it to the shape the angel would have to take, so the answer is not finished here.

**The demand for an angel.**

The people of Makkah used to ask, if the Prophet was appointed to convey God’s message, why God’s angels were not with him to testify. (Why hath not an angel been sent down unto him?) to testify for what he is saying. These disbelievers said, ‘We will believe if Allah sends down an angel with Muhammad ﷺ who speaks to us and bears witness that he is a messenger’. And they say ‘Why has an angel not been sent down to him?’ to Muhammad to confirm his truthfulness; yet had We sent down an angel as they have requested and if they then did not believe the matter that they be destroyed would have been decreed and then they would not be given any respite they would not be given any extra time for repentance or an excuse as is God’s custom in dealing with those before them destroying them when they disbelieve after their request is granted. The second answer to this problem with them was given in the fourth verse in a different manner where it was said that people asking such questions were certainly strange people who were demanding that angels should come down to them.

**The judgement, and the respite that ends.**

(If We sent down an angel) as they are asking you, (then the matter would be judged) he would come down to punish them and take away their souls; it is also said that this means: if the angel comes down, he would destroy all of them; (no further time would be allowed them (for reflection) they would not be allowed any delay. (We send not the angels down except with the truth (i.e. for torment, etc.), and in that case, they (the disbelievers) would have no respite!)[15:8], and,. Since they would be given no respite after that hap-pens, therefore, they should understand that the fact of not showing the miracle demanded by them spells out real good for them, without which they would be nowhere. If we send down an angel of the kind they wish, we will destroy them if they do not believe; and they will not be given time to repent.

**The destruction such a demand invites.**

One answer Allah gave to them was that by making such demands, these heedless people were inviting their own destruction, because the Divine law is that, should a people ask their prophet to show a miracle of their choice, and as a result of their demand, such miracle is shown by the power and will of Allah, then, should they, even then, remain reluctant to believe and accept faith any longer, they are destroyed by a mass general punishment. In other words, it means If We do send the miracle they demand, that is, send an angel, then, these people who are not the kind who would accept truth will still act contrary and hostile even after having seen the miracle, then, the Divine command to have them destroyed would stand activated. These particular people of Makkah were really not making their demands as based on any good intentions, which may have at the least given some hope of their accepting the truth.

**Mercy, and the shape a messenger takes.**

It is a mercy from Allah to His creation that He sends every type of creation, Messengers from among their kind, so that they are able to call their people to Allah, and their people able to talk to them, ask them and benefit from them. The second form in which the angel could come down is that the angel comes in human shape and form, as Sayyidna Jibra'il al-Amin has come to the Holy Prophet several times in the shape of a human being. If the preacher of God’s word appears in the shape of an ordinary man, the ‘reason’ given for ignoring him could be that his effectiveness hinges on a talent for leadership and has nothing to do with Truth or righteousness.

**The mockery and the punishment that followed.**

After having answered all these hostile questions, solace has been given to the Holy Prophet in the fifth verse by saying that this attitude of mockery and injury directed against him by his people is not something particular to him. Finally, what happened was that those who used to mock were overtaken by the punishment which they mocked at. (And indeed Messengers were mocked before you, but their scoffers were surrounded by the very thing that they used to mock at.) comforts the Messenger concerning the denial of him by his people. Allah sent torment, afflictions and punishment on them in this life, as well as the painful torment in the Hereafter, while saving His Messengers and believing servants.

9.text:
The verse takes the condition from the one before it and follows it to its end. And if We had sent an angel, We would have certainly made it assume the form of a man: the angel would not have come as the askers imagined, and the form of a man is named as the shape the sending would have taken. The reason is left for the reader to gather from what follows, since a messenger who comes as a man looks like the messengers who have already been sent, and the demand was made precisely to have something other than a man. Then the last phrase: leaving them more confused than they already are. The confusion is not an accident of the sending but its result, and the wording places it on the people rather than on the message. The verse is short and it closes the argument that the two verses before it opened, so the three of them read as one answer, the book, the angel, and the man. The order matters, since the reader is taken from the demand through the condition to the condition's own end, and at no point is the demand granted. The verses that follow turn from the sign to the mocking of the messengers, so this verse stands at the end of one movement and at the beginning of another.

**An angel in the form of a man.**

And had We appointed him the one who is sent down to them an angel We would assuredly have made him the angel a man that is We would have sent him in the form of a man so that they would be able to see him since no human being is capable of seeing an angel; and had We sent him down and made him a man We would have assuredly confused obscured for them what they are confusing for themselves when they say ‘This is but a mere mortal like the rest of you’. (Had We appointed an angel) as Our messenger, (We assuredly had made him a man) in the form of a man such that they are able to look at him; (and (thus) obscured for them) the real form of the angel they obscure) the traits and description of Muhammad. Ad-Dahhak said that Ibn 'Abbas said about the Ayah [6:9 above], "If an angel was sent to them, he would come in the shape of a man. The second form in which the angel could come down is that the angel comes in human shape and form, as Sayyidna Jibra'il al-Amin has come to the Holy Prophet several times in the shape of a human being.

**The confusion they made for themselves.**

(And had We appointed him an angel, We indeed would have made him a man, and We would have certainly caused them confusion in a matter which they have already covered with confusion.) meaning, if We send an angel along with the human Messenger, or if We send an angel as a Messenger to mankind, he would be in the shape of a man so that they would be able to speak to him and benefit from his teachings. In this case, the angel (in the shape of a human) will also cause confusion for them, just as the confusion they caused themselves over accepting humans as Messengers! (... and We would have certainly caused them confusion in a matter which they have already covered with confusion.) meaning, We would confuse them over their confusion. This is because they will not be able to look at the angel due to light." They assess him on the basis of his outward appearance and, finding him insignificant in that respect, they deny him.

**Why an ordinary man was sent.**

If the preacher of God’s word appears in the shape of an ordinary man, the ‘reason’ given for ignoring him could be that his effectiveness hinges on a talent for leadership and has nothing to do with Truth or righteousness. God’s Messenger appears to them like an ordinary man suddenly emerging and claiming very high status. (And they say: "Why has not an angel been sent down to him?") to convey the Message with admonition along with him. (We send not the angels down except with the truth (i.e. for torment, etc.), and in that case, they (the disbelievers) would have no respite!)[15:8], and,. If I had sent an angel to them, I would have made him in the form of a man, so that they could listen and learn from him, as they would not be able to learn from an angel in the original form that I created him. Therefore, it was said: ‌ ‌ (And had We sent down an angel, the whole matter would have been finished).

10.text:
The verse sets the experience of the Prophet beside the experience of the messengers who came before him. Other messengers had already been ridiculed before you O Prophet: the ridicule is named as something that has happened before, so the treatment he is receiving is not a sign that his mission has failed, and the order of the words puts the messengers first and the mocking second. Then the verse turns from the mockers to the end of the mocking: but those who mocked them were overtaken by what they used to ridicule. Overtaken is the word for being reached by something that a person cannot outrun, and what they used to ridicule is named as the very thing that reaches them, so the punishment is not described in detail but is left as the thing they made fun of. The two halves answer the feeling that comes when what a person carries is refused, and the answer is not an argument but a record: this is how it has gone before, and this is how it ends. The verses that come before had dealt with the demand for a sign and with the confusion that would follow its granting, and this verse closes that passage by moving from the sign to the treatment of the one who brings it. The verses that follow turn to what the mockers should look at in the land and in the ruins of those before them, so the reader is carried from the comfort given to the messenger to the lesson given to his people.

**Messengers were mocked before you.**

If these people poke fun at you by asking for an angel to be sent down with you, then communities in the past also poked fun at their messengers. (And indeed Messengers were mocked before you, but their scoffers were surrounded by the very thing that they used to mock at.) comforts the Messenger concerning the denial of him by his people. Other prophets and messengers before him had to face similar heart-breaking experiences, but they did not lose hope.

**The punishment that surrounded them.**

(Messengers (of Allah) have been derided before thee) their people derided them as your people are deriding you now, (but that whereat they scoffed surrounded) befell (such of them) of the unbelievers (as did deride) the punishment of their derision. Then the punishment, which they used to deny and mock when they were warned about it, surrounded them. Allah sent torment, afflictions and punishment on them in this life, as well as the painful torment in the Hereafter, while saving His Messengers and believing servants.

**The consolation given to the Prophet.**

And messengers were indeed mocked before you — this is meant as a consolation for the Prophet s — but those who scoffed at them were encompassed by that which they mocked namely by the punishment sent down on them those who mock you will be encompassed likewise. In short, the Holy Prophet has been assured that his mission is to convey the commandments of Allah. Whether someone is affected by the message or not, that is not for him to worry about - for it is not a part of his duty as a Messenger of Allah.

**The truth that is veiled, and the day it is lifted.**

This is because God has ordained that the Truth be veiled in doubt, so that man may find reasons for rejecting it alongside arguments in support of its acceptance. These particular people of Makkah were really not making their demands as based on any good intentions, which may have at the least given some hope of their accepting the truth. The Ayah also promises the Messenger , and his believers, of Allah's victory and the good end in this life and the Hereafter. The difference is that for the rest of the world, His grace is fully in evidence right from the first day, whereas for the world of human beings, His grace will be fully shown on the Day of Judgement. (Say: "Travel in the land and see what was the end of those who rejected truth.") meaning, contemplate about yourselves and think about the afflictions Allah struck the previous nations with, those who defied His Messengers and denied them.

11.text:
Say, Travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers. The verse is one sentence and one command, and its force is in the two verbs it gives the reader to carry out. Travel throughout the land is an order to move and to look, and the travel is not named for its own sake but because the ground itself keeps the record, since the places where peoples once lived, their fields and their remains, are the page a person is being sent to read. and see the fate of the deniers: the seeing is the second half of the command, and it is the kind of seeing that ends in knowledge rather than in a glance, since what is placed in front of the traveller is the end of a story rather than a scene. The deniers are named as the people whose end is being shown, and the word covers those who turned away from the messengers, so the reader who is asked to travel is being shown his own danger in another people's ruin. The verse is addressed to the Prophet and through him to those who were arguing with him, so the command is given to the people who had refused rather than to strangers. The order of the two verbs matters, since the travelling comes before the seeing and the seeing comes before any conclusion, and the verse does not say what the traveller will feel when he arrives. It leaves the lesson to be drawn from the ruin itself, and that is how the passage has been working from its first verses, where the destruction of peoples who held more than those who came after them was set out as a thing to be looked at rather than argued about. The verses that follow turn to a question about who owns the heavens and the earth, so the command to travel stands as a bridge between the account of the past and the argument about the present.

**The command to travel, and those who deny.**

(Travel in the land, and see) and reflect upon (the nature of the consequence for the rejecters!) what happened to those who denied Allah and His messengers. "Travel in the land and see what was the end of those who rejected truth. Travel on earth and then think about what happened to those who disbelieved in Allah’s messengers. Say, O Messenger, to these people who deny and mock you:

**The fate of those who denied.**

Say to them ‘Travel in the land and see the nature of the consequence for the deniers’ of the messengers how they were destroyed through chastisement; perhaps they will take heed. (Say: "Travel in the land and see what was the end of those who rejected truth.") meaning, contemplate about yourselves and think about the afflictions Allah struck the previous nations with, those who defied His Messengers and denied them.

**The punishment that came to them.**

Allah sent torment, afflictions and punishment on them in this life, as well as the painful torment in the Hereafter, while saving His Messengers and believing servants. Allah’s punishment fell upon them after they were in a position of strength and power. One answer Allah gave to them was that by making such demands, these heedless people were inviting their own destruction, because the Divine law is that, should a people ask their prophet to show a miracle of their choice, and as a result of their demand, such miracle is shown by the power and will of Allah, then, should they, even then, remain reluctant to believe and accept faith any longer, they are destroyed by a mass general punishment. Consequently, even if the angels descend, while the disbelievers still had the same attitude, then the torment will surely befall them from Allah as a consequence.

12.text:
Ask them, O Prophet: the verse begins with a question placed in the Prophet's mouth, and the asking is aimed at people who already knew the answer. To whom belongs everything in the heavens and the earth, Say, To Allah: the question takes in the whole of the created order and every thing within it, so nothing is left outside the answer, and the answer is given rather than waited for, since the sources notice that this was deliberate and that the people being asked did not deny it, so the point of the question is to make them say with their own tongues what their worship denied. He has taken upon Himself to be Merciful: the mercy is named as something the Lord has bound Himself to, which is a way of speaking about generosity that no one has a right to demand, and the words come here to soften the warning that follows and to give the people time. He will certainly gather all of you together for the Day of Judgment: the gathering is stated as certain, and all of you closes the door on any exception, so the same company that is being questioned is the company that will be assembled. about which there is no doubt: the phrase is repeated across the book, and it belongs to the same purpose, since the day is announced as a fact that does not depend on being believed. But those who have ruined themselves will never believe: the last clause names the reason the announcement will not be received, and the ruin is placed on the people themselves, since the loss is what their own hands have done. The verse moves from a question about ownership to an announcement of mercy and then to the gathering, and it ends by naming those who will not hear it, so the reader is given the whole case in one passage. The verse before it had sent the reader to travel the land and look at the fate of the deniers, and this verse answers the question of who is the master of everything the traveller sees.

**The question and the answer.**

Say to them, O Messenger, ‘To whom does dominion of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, belong? (Unto whom belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth) of created beings? If they answer you, fine; if not, (Say: Unto Allah) belongs the creation of the heavens and the earth. In the opening verse , the disbelievers have been asked as to who is the Master of the entire universe and all that it contains. Then, Allah Himself gives the answer through the blessed words of the Holy Prophet that Allah is the Master of all. The reason for answering the question, rather than waiting for the disbelievers to answer it, is that the answer given was an accepted fact with the disbelievers of Makkah as well, for they were, though involved with Shirk and idolatry, no deniers of the fact that Allah Al-mighty was the Master of the heavens and the earth and everything they contained.

**The mercy He has taken upon Himself.**

He has prescribed He has decreed for Himself mercy as a bounty from Him — this is a gentle summoning of them to the faith. As for the sentence: ‌ (He has prescribed for Himself to be merciful) appearing a little earlier in verse 12, a narration from Sayyidna Abu Hurairah in the Sahih of Muslim reports that the Holy Prophet said: When Allah Ta la made His creation, He made a promise to Himself in writing which is with Him, written in which are the words: that is, My mercy shall remain dominant over My wrath.' (Qurtubi) (When Allah created the creation, He wrote in a Book that He has with Him above the Throne; 'My mercy overcomes My anger.') Allah said;. (He hath prescribed for Himself mercy) for the Community of Muhammad ﷺ in deferring His punishment, (that He may bring you all together) by Allah, He will bring you all together (to a Day) to the Day of Judgement (whereof there is no doubt. Those who ruin their own souls) as well as their dwellings, servants and spouses in Paradise (will not believe) in Muhammad and the Qur'an. He has established mercy upon Himself out of grace for His servants, and will therefore not rush to punish them. Before He began to create the newly arrived things and to originate the engendered beings, He struck the coin of mercy in the mint of the Unseen as the hard cash of the servants' states and deeds: Let me be instructed to clothe them in the shirt of Your mercy, for You have said, 'We sent thee only as a mercy to the worlds' [21:107]. Turn Your promise of mercy and generosity into reality, for You Yourself said, 'O My servants who have been immoderate against yourselves, despair not of God's mercy' [39:53].

**The gathering on the Day of Judgment.**

He will surely gather you together on the Day of Resurrection of which there is no doubt no uncertainty in order to requite you for your deeds. He will surely gather you towards a day of doom) has been used either in the sense of tawaffa meaning to take in full, bring to a finish, or gather, (as in the translation of the meaning given here), in which case, it would mean that Allah Ta ala will gather everyone, from the beginning to the end, on the day of Qiyamah - or, it could mean to gather in the graves,' in which case, it would mean that human beings will be kept being gathered into their resting places unto the day of Qiyamah when they will be raised back to life. (Indeed He will gather you together on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.) swearing by His Most Honored Self that He will gather His servants,. " Tomorrow on the Day of Mustering, the Messenger will call out at the top of the bazaar of the resurrection: O Lord, do not shame MuḤammad in this gathering of the multitudes!

**The souls that were lost, and the mercy they left.**

Those who have forfeited their own souls this is the subject — by exposing them to the chastisement — they do not believe this is the predicate. The sentence which appears at the end of the verse: ‌ (Those who have brought loss to themselves ...) indicates that the deprivation of the disbelievers from the universal mercy of Allah Almighty mentioned earlier was caused by their own deeds, for they did not take to the way which brings mercy - that is, the way of belief and faith. Those who have lost their souls by bringing them to the point of destruction, due to their disbelief in Allah, will not believe and rescue their souls from loss. (Those who destroy themselves) on the Day of Resurrection,. (will not believe.) in the Return and thus do not fear the repercussions of that Day. Those who destroy themselves will not believe And to Him belongs whatsoever exists in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Allah states that He is the King and Owner of the heavens and earth and all of what is in them, and that He has written mercy on His Most Honorable Self. (And whoever is moved away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise, he indeed is successful.)[3:185], success here indicates acquiring profit and negates loss.

**The doubt that is torn down.**

The real test of man is that he should be able to tear down the veil of doubt and raise himself to the position of certainty. He should eschew doubt in all its guises and take a firm hold of the divine Truth. Is there a combination of opposites in God’s regime, given that He seems to have filled man’s world with oppression and injustice and the rest of the world with mercy and meaningfulness? (For appointed meeting of a known Day.)[56:50], the Day of Resurrection that will certainly occur, and there is no doubt for His believing servants in this fact.

13.text:
To Him belongs whatever exists in the day and night. The verse takes the ownership announced in the one before it and gives it a reach in time, since the day and the night cover everything that lives and moves, and the phrase puts the whole of the created order under one hand without exception. And He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing: the two names close the verse and they answer a question the reader has not asked out loud, namely whether the One who owns everything also notices everything. The Hearing is named first because the verse is spoken, and the words people say about their Lord are the first thing that reaches Him, and the Knowing then widens what is heard to include what has not been spoken at all. The order of the two phrases matters, since the ownership is stated first as a fact about the world, and the two names then make that fact personal for the reader. The verse is short and it stands at the head of a passage, and the verses after it turn to the commands given to the Prophet, so this verse works as the ground those commands are built on. The night and the day are named here rather than the heavens and the earth, and there is a reason for the change, since the passage has moved from the wide scene to the time a person actually lives through, and the reader is asked to notice that no hour of his life stands outside the ownership.

**What belongs to Him in the night and the day.**

The word, sukun' appearing in verse 13: ‌ (And to Him belongs what finds rest in the night and the day) could either mean the state of being still or at rest, in which case, the verse would mean that Allah is the Master of everything present in the night and the day. Or, it is also possible that the sense could be that of a combined state of stillness and movement (which would amount to saying - what tarries and what moves), but what was mentioned here is the state of sukun or rest only - because, movement which stands in contrast to it can be understood as being obvious enough. (And to Him belongs whatsoever exists in the night and the day.) meaning, all creatures in the heavens and earth are Allah's servants and creatures, and they are all under His authority, power and will; there is no deity worthy of worship except Him,. Whatever rests hidden in the night and whatever moves about openly in the day are all His servants and His creation: they are all under His domination and control.

**The Hearer and the Knower.**

And to Him exalted be He belongs all that inhabits resides in the night and the day that is to say everything — He is its Lord its Creator and its Possessor; and He is the Hearer of what is said the Knower’ of what is done. (Unto Him belongeth whatsoever resteth in the night and the day. He is the Hearer) of their saying, (the Knower) of their punishment and of the provisions of created beings.

**The night and the day themselves.**

It has been said that night is a general darkness that appears around the world, and day is a general brightness that reaches the whole world. Before the creation of the world and before the creation of light and darkness, there was neither night nor day. In paradise there is no sun, but all is day, for in reality the general brightness is there. God, who is the Lord of Heaven and earth, is also the Lord of that creature who toils during the day and rests at night.

**The light that reaches the heart.**

And He is the Hearing of the moans of the yearners, and the Knowing of the longing of the finders. Whatever is closer to God has a more complete light and luminosity. ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd said, "Surely there is no day or night with your Lord- He illuminates the heavens with the light of His face. " It is mentioned in the traditions that the Lord of the Worlds created a tremendous angel, plac ing night in one of his fists and day in the other. "I placed the disk of the sun in the fist of the angel, but I did not give the hearts of My friends to anyone. " Know that the disk of the sun is in the fist of the angel, but the heart of the lovers is in the fist of the King-majestic and high is He!

**The light that reaches the heart.**

Whatever is closer to God has a more complete light and luminosity. ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd said, "Surely there is no day or night with your Lord- He illuminates the heavens with the light of His face. " It is mentioned in the traditions that the Lord of the Worlds created a tremendous angel, plac ing night in one of his fists and day in the other.
